Re-measured over all 471 engaged nodes: floor median 3, p99 14, worst case 22, and the worst case had moved from Indra to Agni, who binds on NODE GROUPS not predicates - at 17 his `thing` and `unresolved-deity` neighbours are never drawn.

defects_found_and_fixed_by_the_lead.defect: A comment in graph_service.py justified omitting ASCRIBES_TO_DEVATA and HAS_DEVATA_DERIVED from PIPELINE_CONSTANT_PREDICATES by asserting 'Neither carries a confidence property at all -- 0 of 882 and 0 of 39'. Measured live: 882 of 882 and 39 of 39 carry confidence = 1.0, matching their already-declared parent HAS_DEVATA_ASCRIPTION (5,385 of 5,385 at 1.0). The comment's stated reason was the exact opposite of the data, and the omission it justified left 921 edges presenting an unearned per-edge confidence on a serving surface.
defects_found_and_fixed_by_the_lead.fix: both declared at 1.0; the false note replaced with the measured counts and the lesson that a comment carrying a measurement goes stale silently because nothing re-measures a comment.

defects_found_and_fixed_by_the_lead.defect: HAS_PARALLEL_PADA (4,079 edges) and RECEIVES_OFFERING (4) were populated but classified neither traversable nor refused-for-a-reason, so /api/v1/graph would not cross them and nothing told a reader the layers existed.
defects_found_and_fixed_by_the_lead.structural_blocker_found_while_implement: HAS_PARALLEL_PADA joins a verse to a PadaParallelGroup, and a verse may contribute more than one pada to the SAME group: 4,079 edges run over only 4,076 distinct (source,type,target) triples. VG:RV:SAK:M01:S097:V001 contributes pada a and pada c to one group, and two more verses do the same. The public relationship id IS that triple, so whitelisting it would publish 6 edges under 3 ids - reintroducing the exact two-objects-one-id defect this pass exists to close.
defects_found_and_fixed_by_the_lead.resolution: RECEIVES_OFFERING declared traversable with a curated PredicateSemantics entry (4 distinct triples, worst=1, clean). HAS_PARALLEL_PADA refused with the measured structural reason stated in NON_TRAVERSABLE_REASONS, and the exact unlock named (the id must carry the pada_key the edges already store). Extending the public relationship id scheme is outside R1.

defects_found_and_NOT_fixed.defect: The /insights/cross-veda SEMANTIC_ASSERTION row is served population_status = NOT_BUILT, which the Lab renders as the mark for 'The layer does not exist anywhere in this graph' - about a layer holding 35,131 nodes. Its per-cell note contradicts itself inside one sentence: 'every one of its assertions is Rigvedic, so it has no non-Rigvedic endpoint to pair with. Measured: 35,131 assertions over AV, RV, SV, YV.' The figure was refreshed; the reasoning clause was not.
defects_found_and_NOT_fixed.measured: 35,131 assertions: RV 27,057 / AV 6,167 / YV 1,543 / SV 364. 8,074 are non-Rigvedic, over 4,080 non-RV mantras. 0 assertions hang off no mantra.
defects_found_and_NOT_fixed.correct_representation: CLASS_NOT_CROSS_VEDA, already in the enum and already used for the analogous PARALLEL_TO row. The layer exists; a semantic assertion is a predication with ONE passage endpoint, so it cannot span two corpora regardless of which corpus its verse is in.
defects_found_and_NOT_fixed.also_wrong: the plate's summary sentence counts it among 'N of the 8 classes are not built at all'
defects_found_and_NOT_fixed.why_not_fixed: it changes a public endpoint's absence vocabulary and invalidates the cross-Veda consumer hash verified this pass; it is outside R1's declared gate set, and R1 is explicitly forbidden from opening another broad campaign. Handed to FINAL_RELEASE_CERTIFICATION already diagnosed.

defects_found_and_NOT_fixed.defect: :SemanticAssertion carries TWO display_type values for one object type - 'SemanticAssertion' on the 4,865 assertion_id nodes and 'SEMANTIC_ASSERTION' on the 30,266 assertion_key nodes - and both reach the shipped world.raw.json. It is the only pair among the artifact's 48 node types differing merely in spelling.
defects_found_and_NOT_fixed.frontend_consequence: frontend/src/lib/knowledge.ts normalizeType() only uppercases, so entityHref() mints TWO routes for one type: /entities/semanticassertion/<id> and /entities/semantic_assertion/<id>. Both resolve (the route is a dynamic [type]/[id] segment), so this is duplicate canonical URLs plus an inconsistent type label rendered to readers in graph-shell.tsx, not a broken link.
defects_found_and_NOT_fixed.why_not_fixed: the root cause is the graph's own display_type split, and the graph is frozen this pass. A frontend fold would hide a data inconsistency that should be repaired at source. The repo's established idiom for this is explicit enumeration of both spellings - INTERNAL_GRAPH_TYPES already lists QAISSUE/QA_ISSUE, SOURCEARTIFACT/SOURCE_ARTIFACT, TEXTVERSION/TEXT_VERSION, PIPELINERUN/PIPELINE_RUN.

defects_found_and_NOT_fixed.defect: The AgentiveAssertionView docstring says 'All 4,865 SemanticAssertion nodes hang off Rigvedic passages.' VERIFIED TRUE as scoped - that population IS entirely Rigvedic (RV 4,865, and its 2,406/2,459 knowledge_layer split matches). But the phrase reads as a claim about the total while 35,131 SemanticAssertion nodes exist, so a reader infers a Rigveda-only layer. Ambiguous scope rather than a wrong figure; it surfaces in the generated frontend/src/lib/api-schema.ts, which must not be hand-edited.
